title: Wind and solar overtake fossil fuels in Germany for the first time ever

content_html:
More of Germany's electricity came from wind and solar power than from fossil fuels for the first time ever in 2025, according to Carbon Brief's analysis of Energy Institute Statistical Review of World Energy data. Wind and solar together generated 225 terawatt hours (TWh) of electricity, 44% of the total, against 217 TWh (43%) from fossil fuels – a milestone Germany shares with the EU as a whole, which also saw wind and solar overtake fossil-fuel generation for the first time in 2025.

Wind and solar generated more electricity than fossil fuels in Germany for the first time ever in 2025. Source: Energy Institute Statistical Review of World Energy, 2026 / Carbon Brief.

The shift reflects two decades of rapid growth in solar and onshore wind under Germany's "Energiewende" strategy, as the country transitions away from both coal and nuclear power. Germany aims to install 115 gigawatts (GW) of onshore wind by 2030, and approved a record 20.8 GW of new capacity in 2025 alone. Official targets require economy-wide net-zero emissions by 2045, an 80% renewables share of electricity consumption by 2030, and a "largely climate neutral" power system by 2035.

Germany has to lean on renewables harder than neighbours such as France and the UK to hit those goals, precisely because of its nuclear phaseout – a core plank of the Energiewende that remains politically settled despite recent pushback. Centre-right Chancellor Friedrich Merz described the phaseout as a "strategic mistake" earlier this year, but his government has ruled out returning to conventional nuclear power. Coal remains the bigger near-term challenge: Germany still relies on it far more than most other European countries, with an official phaseout deadline of "no later than" 2038, though experts believe the country is on track to eliminate coal from its power supply years ahead of that date despite pressure during the recent energy crisis to slow the transition.

Renewables now face a different kind of opposition, however: mounting resistance from the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), even as the current coalition simultaneously pursues new gas-fired power plants of its own – legislated as a bridge technology, with the plants intended to convert to run on green hydrogen by 2045 to stay consistent with the climate-neutrality target. Very few voices outside the AfD are calling to scrap the coal phaseout altogether, but the government is due to publish a review of its timelines in August, which will be the next test of how firmly Berlin intends to hold the line.

content_html_zh:
根据 Carbon Brief 对能源研究所《世界能源统计评论》数据的分析，到 2025 年，德国来自风能和太阳能的电力将首次超过来自化石燃料的电力。 风能和太阳能合计发电量为 225 太瓦时 (TWh)，占总发电量的 44%，而化石燃料发电量为 217 太瓦时 (TWh)（43%）——这是德国与整个欧盟共同的里程碑，风能和太阳能发电量也将在 2025 年首次超过化石燃料发电。

2025 年，德国风能和太阳能发电量将首次超过化石燃料。 资料来源：能源研究所世界能源统计回顾，2026 年/Carbon Brief。

这一转变反映了德国“能源转型”战略下太阳能和陆上风电二十年来的快速增长，该国逐渐摆脱煤炭和核电。 德国的目标是到 2030 年安装 115 吉瓦 (GW) 的陆上风电，并仅在 2025 年就批准了创纪录的 20.8 吉瓦新装机容量。 官方目标要求到 2045 年实现整个经济体的净零排放，到 2030 年可再生能源在电力消耗中所占比例达到 80%，到 2035 年实现“基本气候中性”的电力系统。

德国必须比法国和英国等邻国更加依赖可再生能源来实现这些目标，正是因为它的核逐步淘汰 — — 这是能源转型的核心支柱，尽管最近遭到阻力，但在政治上仍然得到了解决。 今年早些时候，中右翼总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨将逐步淘汰描述为“战略错误”，但他的政府已排除恢复常规核电的可能性。 煤炭仍然是近期面临的更大挑战：德国仍然比大多数其他欧洲国家更加依赖煤炭，官方的逐步淘汰期限“不迟于”2038年，尽管专家认为，尽管最近的能源危机期间面临减缓转型的压力，但专家相信德国有望提前数年从电力供应中消除煤炭。

然而，可再生能源现在面临着另一种反对：极右翼的德国另类选择党 (AfD) 的阻力越来越大，尽管目前的联盟同时也在寻求自己的新燃气发电厂——作为过渡技术进行立法，这些发电厂计划到 2045 年转变为使用绿色氢来运行，以与气候中和目标保持一致。 德国选择党之外几乎没有人呼吁完全废除煤炭淘汰计划，但政府将于八月份发布对其时间表的审查，这将是柏林打算如何坚定地坚持这一立场的下一个考验。
